# Cowtext — Sound Design (v1)

The sound bible: aesthetic direction, full cue sheet, mixing rules, file specs, and the
plan for replacing placeholders with crafted SFX. Companion to
[`DESIGN_SPEC.md`](DESIGN_SPEC.md); events come from plan §8, playback runtime is
**howler.js** (Phase 5 — not installed yet). Placeholders are generated by
[`../../scripts/gen_sfx.py`](../../scripts/gen_sfx.py) into `assets/sfx/` with a
`cues.json` manifest of measured stats.

## 1. Aesthetic direction

**Sound is the barn's voice — the audio equivalent of Silkscreen.** The design spec bans
sound on routine UI events; almost everything below is driven by *what the cow does*, not
what the user clicks. Same rule as visuals: tool-layer sound = state changed; barn sound =
the cow moved.

The palette is a 16-bit console fantasy, played warm:

- **Chip voices, console mix.** Square, triangle, and noise channels — but every square
  goes through a lowpass so it reads as "SNES cartridge", not "smoke alarm". Warm, never
  shrill: nothing carries significant energy above ~5 kHz.
- **Short envelopes.** Fast attacks (0.5–15 ms), exponential decays. No pads, no reverb
  tails. The longest one-shot is the ding at 0.7 s; most cues live under 300 ms.
- **Pentatonic-friendly pitches.** All tuned cues sit in A-minor / C-major pentatonic
  (A, C, D, E, G) so overlapping cues can never clash harmonically. Mechanical cues
  (clacks, slides, shuffles) are noise-based and pitch-free.
- **The cow is low, the machine is high.** The moo lives at G2–C3 in detuned triangles;
  bells and confirms live at A4–A5. Register separates the mascot from the machinery.
- **Quiet by profession.** This app sits next to a terminal all day. Everything is mixed
  several notches below game-default loudness; the ambient bed is barely there. The sound
  should be missable, and missed when muted.

## 2. Cue sheet

Fourteen cues. Durations, peaks, and RMS are the measured values of the current
placeholders (see `assets/sfx/cues.json`).

### Barn cues (plan §8 event map) — Phase 5

| Cue | File | Trigger (BarnEvent) | Dur | Character | Tier | Must NOT play when |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Keyboard clack | `kb_clack.wav` | `prompt_submitted` | 0.10 s | one soft mechanical key: HP-noise burst + 1.9 kHz tick, faint second key | Action −9 | more than 1× per prompt; during calm/mute |
| Drawer slide | `drawer_slide.wav` | `read` → cabinet prop (`rules`/`persona`) | 0.26 s | darkening noise sweep (2.6 k→0.7 kHz) + low wooden thunk at end | Action −11 | read-burst throttle active (§3); node already open |
| Page flip | `page_flip.wav` | `read` → bookshelf prop (`architecture`/`reference`) | 0.15 s | two feather-light HP-noise flicks | Texture −13 | read-burst throttle active |
| Paper shuffle | `paper_shuffle.wav` | `read` → corkboard/crate (`task`/`workflow`) | 0.28 s | four soft LP-noise puffs, rising slightly | Texture −13 | read-burst throttle active |
| Typewriter | `typewriter.wav` | `edit`/`write` — **loop** while the cow's typing animation runs | 0.50 s/bar | four keystrikes per bar (noise + detuned ticks), seamless loop | Action −10 | animation not visible; longer than 3 s continuous (fade out, keep animation) |
| Ding | `ding.wav` | `edit`/`write` completes (paper stack +1) | 0.70 s | typewriter bell: A5 triangle+sine partial, warm ring | Confirm −10 | the typewriter loop didn't run first; more than 1× per 2 s |
| Soft sniff | `sniff.wav` | `grep`/`glob` | 0.22 s | two tiny dark LP-noise air puffs (650/550 Hz) | Whisper −16 | within 1 s of the previous sniff (searches come in volleys) |
| Ambient loop | `ambient_loop.wav` | waiting > 5 s — **loop**, fade in 800 ms | 2.0 s/loop | A1+A2+E3 sine drone with slow swells + faint hay-wind noise bed; seamless | Bed −18 | any one-shot pending; fades out immediately on the next event |
| Happy moo | `moo_happy.wav` | `stop` (turn done, cow trots back) | 0.55 s | two-note moo G2→C3, ±6-cent detuned triangle pair + octave head-voice, 5.5 Hz vibrato, LP 1.4 kHz | **Hero −7** | on `SubagentStop` (that's the calf's cue); more than 1× per turn |
| Calf spawn | `calf_spawn.wav` | subagent spawns (calf enters) | 0.18 s | rising soft-square blip E5→A5 | Texture −13 | >2 calves spawn within 1 s (play once for the batch) |
| Calf despawn | `calf_despawn.wav` | `SubagentStop` (calf leaves) | 0.18 s | falling soft-square blip A5→E5 | Texture −13 | same batch rule as spawn |

### Tool-layer cues (state changes only — never routine UI) 

The design spec bans sound on routine UI events. Exactly three tool-layer moments qualify
as *state changed* and get a cue; nothing else in the editor ever sounds (no hovers, no
clicks, no toasts, no node selection, no keystrokes).

| Cue | File | Trigger | Dur | Character | Tier | Must NOT play when |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Compile written | `compile_ok.wav` | diff **approved and file written** to disk | 0.34 s | two-note confirm C5→G5, lowpassed square | Confirm −10 | dry-run / compile-to-clipboard; diff cancelled; any write failed (that's error's job) |
| Assemble done | `assemble_done.wav` | a node's `claude -p` run succeeds (green flash) | 0.55 s | rising pentatonic arpeggio A4–C5–E5, triangle chimes | Confirm −10 | batch assemble: play once when the *queue* drains, not per node |
| Problem surfaced | `error_soft.wav` | problems count goes 0 → n (cycle, missing file, failed write, dead hook) | 0.32 s | low muted double-knock, falling triangles 150→92 Hz + felt noise | Action −11 | count merely increases (n → n+1); within 10 s of the last one; concerned, never alarming — no red-alert klaxon exists in this app |

Phase mapping: the three tool-layer cues can technically ship with Phases 2–3, but
**no sound plays before the sound settings + mute + calm mode exist**. Simplest honest
sequencing: all audio lands in Phase 5 together with the toggles (feature 7.6, "day one
of sound").

## 3. Mixing rules

### Volume hierarchy (baked into masters + runtime gain)

Masters are normalized to per-tier peaks; howler group gains then scale whole tiers,
so re-mixing is a settings change, not a re-render.

| Tier | Master peak | Cues | Runtime group |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hero | −7 dBFS | moo_happy | `barn` |
| Confirm | −10 dBFS | ding, compile_ok, assemble_done | `barn` / `tool` |
| Action | −9…−11 dBFS | kb_clack, drawer_slide, typewriter, error_soft | `barn` / `tool` |
| Texture | −13 dBFS | page_flip, paper_shuffle, calf_spawn, calf_despawn | `barn` |
| Whisper | −16 dBFS | sniff | `barn` |
| Bed | −18 dBFS | ambient_loop | `ambient` |

Global ceiling: no master ever peaks above −1 dBFS (enforced by the generator script).
Default master volume ships at 60%.

### Ducking

- **Ambient bed ducks under everything**: −6 dB while any one-shot or the typewriter loop
  plays; recovers over 400 ms. On any new BarnEvent the bed fades out in 250 ms (the barn
  woke up).
- **The moo ducks the barn**: while `moo_happy` plays, all other currently-sounding cues
  duck −12 dB. The turn-complete moment belongs to the cow.
- Nothing ducks the tool-layer confirms — they're short and share no register with the
  moo.

### Concurrency & throttling

- **Max 3 simultaneous one-shot voices** + 1 typewriter loop + 1 ambient bed. A fourth
  one-shot steals the oldest voice (howler: fixed pool, track ids).
- **Read-burst throttle**: agents read files in volleys. At most one read cue
  (drawer/flip/shuffle) per **150 ms**; a burst of ≥ 4 reads inside 500 ms collapses to a
  single `paper_shuffle` and stays silent until the burst ends. The canvas pulse still
  shows every read — sound summarizes, visuals enumerate.
- Per-cue cooldowns as listed in the cue sheet (sniff 1 s, ding 2 s, error 10 s).
- **Never queue sound.** Animations queue (plan §8); audio does not. A cue that can't
  play now is dropped, not delayed — late sound is wrong sound.

### Mute, calm mode, focus

- **Mute** (toggle, day one): silences everything instantly (hard stop, no fade-out
  longer than 50 ms). Animations continue.
- **Calm mode** (plan §8, spec: one control, both effects): no sound **and** reduced
  motion. Mute is implied; the toggle also drops pulses/marches per the reduced-motion
  spec. `prefers-reduced-motion` at the OS level force-enables calm mode's motion half
  but only *suggests* muting (sound stays a separate user choice).
- **Hidden/unfocused window**: all sound suspends when the window is hidden or minimized
  (pairs with the Pixi pause guard, feature 7.7). An unfocused-but-visible window keeps
  sounding — watching the barn from the corner of your eye is the point of the app.
- **View toggle**: barn cues play in **both** Canvas and Barn views once Phase 5 lands
  (the live pulse and the drawer sound describe the same event); tool-layer cues play
  everywhere. Settings exposes three switches: master volume, "Barn sounds", "Tool
  sounds" — plus Mute and Calm mode.

## 4. File & format specs

- **Masters**: 44.1 kHz, 16-bit PCM WAV, **mono**. Mono is deliberate: cues are diegetic
  barn sounds and may later be panned at runtime by prop position; baked stereo would
  fight that.
- **Peak per tier** as in §3; every file ends at digital silence (edge fades kill
  clicks). Each file ≤ 200 KB (longest is the 2.0 s ambient loop at ~176 KB).
- **Loops** (`typewriter.wav`, `ambient_loop.wav`) must be seamless at the file boundary:
  the ambient loop is rendered long and equal-power crossfaded onto its own head; the
  typewriter bar is exactly 0.5 s with all strikes fully decayed inside the bar.
- **Naming**: `snake_case.wav`, named for the sound, not the event (`ding.wav`, not
  `write_complete.wav`) — events remap, sounds don't.
- **Manifest**: `assets/sfx/cues.json` — duration, peak, RMS, loop flag, bytes per cue.
  Regenerated by the script; treat as read-only.
- **Licensing**: placeholders are procedurally generated in-repo (no external samples, no
  license burden). When CC0/purchased sounds arrive, record them in the asset licence
  manifest (feature 7.8).

### Howler sprite plan (Phase 5)

- Concatenate the **12 one-shots** into a single `sfx_sprite` file with 300 ms silence
  gaps, exported as `.webm` + `.mp3` fallback for shipping (WAV masters stay in-repo as
  the source). One `Howl` with a `sprite:` map — `{ ding: [offsetMs, durMs] }` — one
  network/disk fetch, zero first-play latency.
- The **two loops stay separate `Howl` instances** (`typewriter`, `ambient`): they need
  independent `loop: true`, fades, and duck automation that sprite segments make awkward.
- Sprite offsets are generated from `cues.json` durations at build time, never
  hand-typed.
- Base64 inlining of audio into source files is banned (CLAUDE.md hard rule) — the sprite
  is a real asset file.

## 5. Placeholder inventory (generated)

`scripts/gen_sfx.py` — Python stdlib only (`wave`, `struct`, `math`, `random`, `json`),
deterministic (seeded noise), self-verifying (fails the run if any cue is silent, clips
the −1 dBFS ceiling, or exceeds 200 KB). Re-run with `python scripts/gen_sfx.py`.

Synthesis parameters per cue:

| File | Recipe |
|---|---|
| `kb_clack.wav` | strike = HP(300)·LP(4 k) noise burst (10 ms decay) + 1.9 kHz sine tick (8 ms); ghost second key at +28 ms, −6 dB |
| `drawer_slide.wav` | noise through swept one-pole LP 2.6 k→0.7 kHz, sine½ amplitude arc, HP 180 Hz; end thunk = 130→95 Hz sine glide, 18 ms decay |
| `page_flip.wav` | two HP-noise flicks: 5.2 kHz/12 ms then 4.2 kHz/22 ms at +55 ms |
| `paper_shuffle.wav` | 4 LP(2.6 k) HP(500) noise puffs, 20 ms decay, ~55–75 ms apart (seeded jitter), rising level |
| `typewriter.wav` | 0.5 s bar; strikes at 0/125/250/375 ms; per-strike tick pitch 1.75–2.3 kHz + noise, level variation |
| `ding.wav` | A5 (880 Hz) triangle LP 3 k, τ = 160 ms + 2nd partial (+7 cents, ×2 freq) at −20 dB + hammer click |
| `sniff.wav` | two LP-noise puffs at 650 Hz/20 ms and 550 Hz/26 ms, 100 ms apart, slow 10–12 ms attacks |
| `moo_happy.wav` | melody G2 hold 200 ms → 60 ms portamento → C3; voices = triangle pair at ±6 cents + octave triangle at −16 dB; vibrato 5.5 Hz, 1.2%; LP 1.4 kHz; env 30 ms attack, 300 ms hold, τ = 100 ms |
| `calf_spawn.wav` | soft-square (LP 2.2 k) E5 (70 ms) → A5 (100 ms) |
| `calf_despawn.wav` | mirror: A5 → E5 |
| `compile_ok.wav` | soft-square (LP 2.6 k) C5 (τ 45 ms) → G5 at +120 ms (τ 70 ms) |
| `assemble_done.wav` | triangle chimes A4, C5, E5 at 110 ms spacing, τ = 80 ms, +2nd-partial sparkle |
| `error_soft.wav` | two LP(≤500) triangle knocks gliding 150→105 Hz and 132→92 Hz, 130 ms apart, felt-noise tap on the second |
| `ambient_loop.wav` | drone A1/A2/E3 sines with 0.5–1 Hz periodic swells + LP(320) noise bed with 0.5 Hz wander; 2.5 s render crossfaded to seamless 2.0 s |

## 6. Replacing placeholders with crafted SFX

When real sounds arrive (chip-tracker renders, Foley, or purchased packs):

1. **Keep the filename and rough duration.** Code and sprite maps key on file stems;
   durations feed animation timing (every animation ≤ 1.5 s). Stay within ±30% of the
   placeholder length; regenerate the sprite map from the new `cues.json`.
2. **Match the tier peak, then trust your ears.** Normalize the master to its tier's
   peak from §3, then A/B against `moo_happy.wav` — the moo is the loudness anchor;
   nothing may feel louder than the moo.
3. **Honor the register split**: cow ≤ C3 territory, machinery ≥ A4. A recorded moo
   pitched into the same G2→C3 gesture will drop in without re-tuning the mix.
4. **Loops must survive the boundary test**: play 10 consecutive loops at full volume —
   any click or level bump fails.
5. **Character over fidelity.** A too-real drawer recording will clash with the pixel
   barn; bitcrush/downsample real recordings toward the 16-bit fantasy before they ship.
   The SNES sound was 32 kHz ADPCM — a little grit is period-correct.
6. Update the asset licence manifest (7.8) and re-run `python scripts/gen_sfx.py`
   **only if regenerating placeholders** — it overwrites all 14 files unconditionally.
